news.headline: Why Forgent Power Solutions (FPS) Failed to Live Up to Its IPO Hype
news.summary: A commentary piece looks at why the stock has fallen back toward its $27 February IPO price, after a July follow-on priced at $49, despite record results. It comes a day after FPS hit a new 1-year low, with no new company-specific news behind the slide.

news.headline: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) Reaches New 1-Year Low
news.summary: Forgent shares fell to a new low since their February IPO, extending the post-earnings slide despite the raised FY2027 guidance. The move follows a run of analyst target cuts, even though insiders have been buying on the open market.

news.headline: Marshall Wace LLP Buys 4,568,499 Shares of Forgent Power Solutions, Inc. $FPS
news.summary: A 13F filing shows hedge fund Marshall Wace built a new position of about 4.57M Forgent shares during the third quarter. The filing reflects positions held before the post-earnings selloff, so it says nothing about current holdings.

news.headline: Baird keeps Outperform on Forgent, lowers price target to $27 from $38
news.summary: Baird kept its Outperform rating but cut its target to $27 from $38, the latest in a string of post-Q1 cuts. Even the reduced target sits well above the roughly $18 close of Nov 20.

news.headline: Director Gregory Spierkel buys 25,000 Forgent shares
news.summary: A Form 4 filed late on Nov 23 shows director Gregory Spierkel bought 25,000 shares in the open market on Nov 20, the day the stock fell 14% to its $18 close. It is the largest purchase yet in the insider buying that followed the post-earnings slide.

news.headline: KeyBanc reiterates Overweight on Forgent Power Solutions
news.summary: On the same day Morgan Stanley trimmed its target, KeyBanc stood by its Overweight rating, keeping it among the bulls on Forgent's data-center and grid-equipment demand. The average 12-month target has slipped to about $42, still roughly double the share price.

news.headline: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) Stock Price Target Cut by Morgan Stanley
news.summary: Morgan Stanley lowered its Forgent price target to $40 from $45 and kept an Equal Weight rating. The shares closed down 14.1% at $18.00 on Friday, just above the Nov 6 all-time low of $17.67, after closing at $20.96 on Nov 19.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q2 2027 results
catalysts.detail: First quarterly check against the raised FY2027 guide of $2.45-2.65B revenue and $587-637M adjusted EBITDA; watch order intake and backlog conversion.

catalysts.label: Columbus office ramp
catalysts.detail: New 90,000 sq ft Columbus, Ohio office adding 85 jobs in support functions.

catalysts.label: Tijuana Powertrain expansion online
catalysts.detail: Expected to raise total revenue capacity to about $5.8B.

pulse: Forgent beat on Nov 12 with record fiscal Q1 revenue of $479M (+69%) and adjusted EBITDA of $105M, and raised its FY2027 guide to $2.45-2.65B revenue, with backlog already covering the full-year guide and hyperscaler orders building through 2028. The stock keeps sliding because the guide midpoint trailed estimates: a wave of target cuts (Wells Fargo $25, Baird $27 on Nov 23, JPMorgan $35, Morgan Stanley $40, TD Cowen $55) sent it down 14% on Nov 20 to an $18.00 close, and on Nov 25 it touched a new post-IPO intraday low of $16.88 before closing at $18.82 (+1%), though KeyBanc reiterated Overweight and Marshall Wace disclosed a new ~4.6M-share stake built in Q3. Insiders have answered with open-market buying (CEO, CFO, directors including Gregory Spierkel with 25,000 shares on Nov 20, the general counsel and the CAO since Nov 16); the next hard checkpoint is fiscal Q2 results around February.
